text:
maya: quick follow-up after the GQA/MQA selection RFC. want to nail down where the "negotiation" lives: scheduler (request routing) vs kernel selector (local runtime). thinking about semantics for fallback + perf hints.

lee: +1. we should separate fast, stateless heuristics from the full selector. cheap precheck at scheduler to avoid cross-queue handoff when unnecessary.

david: agree, but watch out for affinity starvation. if scheduler rejects a request because it thinks MQA will be slow, we could end up routing too many to GQA and saturating it. need a soft quota or token bucket.

maya: exactly. proposal sketch:
- scheduler runs a micro-heuristic that outputs a KernelHint (GQA/MQA/ANY) + confidence score (0-1).
- kernel selector can override based on live queue/backpressure and per-model kernel capabilities.
- when there's disagreement, use priority: selector override if confidence < 0.6? or if queue depth > threshold.

sukh: proto suggestion for KernelHint (very small):
```proto
message KernelHint {
  enum Mode {
    UNKNOWN = 0;
    GQA = 1;
    MQA = 2;
    ANY = 3;
  }
  Mode mode = 1;
  float confidence = 2; // 0..1
  repeated string tags = 3; // e.g. ["short_seq", "high_entropy"]
}
```
This keeps scheduler <-> selector contract tiny.

rachel: ran a quick perf sim with live trace (30m) using a soft-quota at scheduler. result: tail latency reduced ~6% for P95 when we allowed selector to override under high load. attaching quick summary: 30m trace, 5k req/s, MQA hit-rate improved from 28% -> 35%, cost delta -2.1% overall.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rolled out to runtime/staging at 2024-11-02T14:12:23Z :rocket:

lee: nice numbers. one implementation detail: selector override needs to be lightweight. avoid a full scheduling decision while holding request locks. maybe use a loan-token: scheduler marks request as "tentative" and puts it on kernel queue with hint; selector can claim or release within X ms.

david: loan-token sounds good. also require stateless fallback path: if selector doesn't respond within X, default to scheduler hint. ensures forward progress.

maya: risks: more protocol complexity, potential jitter around toggling between kernels for similar requests. mitigation: hysteresis on hints (sticky for N requests / seconds) + telemetry to detect oscillation.

sukh: telemetry payloads we need: hint_origin (scheduler/selector), hint_confidence, final_kernel, override_reason, queue_depth_at_decision. small but critical.

maya: action items:
1) @sukh draft a tiny proto PR for KernelHint + token handshake.
2) @rachel run a 2h sim with loan-token + hysteresis knobs.
3) @lee prototype selector-side fast-path override (no locks).
4) me: write RFC addendum with decision matrix and toggles.

rachel: will do 2h sim tomorrow morning, include per-model slices. :+1:

maya: cool. if no objections i'll file the addendum by EOD. thanks all.
